content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps correspond to forward reactions: 1) amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic steps: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and aniline; break α,β-unsaturated acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid (or maybe the unsaturated acid is product of Doebner from aldehyde). And break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and aniline.

Thus target has: a para-methyl phenyl attached to sulfonamide linking to another phenyl ring bearing the α,β-unsaturated amide side chain.

Structure: p-tolyl-sulfonamide attached to phenyl-sulfonyl group (SO2) attached to phenyl ring which has para-substituted with the α,β-unsaturated amide chain (C=C-CO-NH-aniline). Actually the SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

So we have two aromatic rings: ring A (tolyl) attached via sulfonamide N to sulfonyl group attached to ring B (phenyl). Ring B has para-substituted with the α,β-unsaturated amide chain (trans). The amide attaches to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So final amide is between carboxylic acid (from Doebner) and aniline.

Thus retrosynthesis:

Step 1 (reverse of amide formation): disconnect amide between carbonyl and aniline. Precursors: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (with phenyl ring B attached) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So product of step 1: α,β-unsaturated acid (call fragment 1) and aniline.

Step 2 (reverse of Doebner): disconnect α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde (on ring B) and malonic acid (or maybe malonic acid derivative). The aldehyde is on ring B para position (CHO). So fragment 1 becomes aldehyde phenyl (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) attached to sulfonyl group? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the same phenyl ring B at position para to the aldehyde? In SMILES, the sulfonyl group is attached to ring B at position 1 (c2ccc(... )cc2). The unsaturated chain is attached at para to sulfonyl? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl. So the aldehyde precursor would be c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to sulfonyl. So we need sulfonyl phenyl aldehyde.

Thus step 2: aldehyde phenyl-sulfonyl (Ar-SO2-Ph-CHO) + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (Ar-SO2-Ph-CH=CH-COOH). So we need template for Doebner modification.

Step 3 (reverse of sulfonamide formation): disconnect sulfonamide N to give sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) and aniline (tolyl-amine). Actually the sulfonamide is between tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring B. So precursors: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-? Actually the sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl B). The sulfonyl chloride is ClSO2-Ph (where phenyl is attached to the unsaturated chain later). So we need ClSO2-Ph-? The sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl B (c2ccc(Cl)cc2?) Actually the sulfonyl chloride would be ClSO2-Ph where the phenyl is the same as ring B (the one bearing the unsaturated chain). So after step 2, we have Ar-SO2-Ph-CH=CH-COOH (where Ar is the tolyl? Wait the sulfonyl group is between the two phenyls: NS(=O)(=O)c2... So the sulfonyl is attached to the tolyl N and to phenyl B. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be ClSO2-Ph-? The phenyl B is attached to sulfonyl on one side, and later will have the unsaturated chain attached at para position. So the sulfonyl chloride is ClSO2-Ph (where the phenyl has a para substituent that will become the unsaturated chain). So we can treat as sulfonyl chloride with phenyl bearing aldehyde (or later unsaturated). So step 3: p-toluidine + phenyl-sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide.

Thus we need to find templates for each step. We have template 401931 which seems to be amide formation (amide from acid and amine). That template's retro_smarts: [#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])=[O;D1;H0:3].O-C(=O)-[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5] . This seems to be reverse of amide formation where the product is amide with conjugated double bond? Actually the forward direction (right to left) is amide + alkene -> acid + something? Not sure. But we can use it for amide formation.

We also need a Doebner template. Search for functional_groups_broken: aldehydes, formed: C-C double bonds, aliphatic carboxylic acid. Let's try search with correct functional group names: broken aldehydes, formed C-C double bonds and aliphatic carboxylic acid.
